members.working:
Identify product hybridization for each reaction.
(i) CoCl2 + NH3 (excess) in air-excluded N2 gives Co(III) ammine complex Co(NH3)3Cl3 (or Co(NH3)6Cl2). Co(III) typically octahedral, hybridization sp3d2.
(ii) SiCl4 + LiAlH4 in ether reduces Si to SiH4 (or Si-H compounds) tetrahedral sp3.
(iii) P4O10 + H2O gives H3PO4 (or H3PO4) tetrahedral sp3.
(iv) B2H6 hydrolysis gives B(OH)3 trigonal planar sp2.
(v) XeF6 + limited H2O gives XeOF4 (square pyramidal) with one lone pair; hybridization is often described as sp3d2 for Xe in XeOF4 (five bonds + lone pair). However limited water may give XeO2F2? Typically XeF6 + H2O → XeOF4 (square pyramidal) which uses sp3d2. But some may argue Xe in XeF6 is d2sp3? However question asks sp3d2 hybridised element in its product. Only reaction (i) clearly gives an octahedral complex with d orbitals involved (Co(III) ammine). XeOF4 also uses d orbitals but common hybridization for Xe in XeOF4 is sp3d2 (five bonds + lone pair). However the phrase "sp³d² hybridised" usually refers to octahedral geometry with six equivalent orbitals. XeOF4 has five equivalent orbitals (square pyramidal) often described as sp3d. But many textbooks say Xe in XeOF4 uses sp3d2? Need decide. Safer: only Co(III) ammine is definitely sp3d2. Thus count = 1.
Thus answer integer 1.
